messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test case `testLang412Left()` fails because it calls `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` passing a `null` string without having set any "null text" to handle null values properly in the `StrBuilder`. The method `appendFixedWidthPadLeft(Object obj, int width, char padChar)` uses `getNullText()` to determine what string to append when the passed object is `null`. From the code, this method has this line:

```java
String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
```

If `getNullText()` returns `null`, then `str` becomes `null`, and the subsequent call to `str.length()` in the next line will trigger a `NullPointerException`.

The current bug report states a null pointer exception occurs when appending a fixed width null value if `getNullText()` has not been set. This matches the root cause in the code where `getNullText()` default value is `null`. The setter `setNullText()` explicitly allows clearing the null text by passing an empty string, turning it into `null` internally.

Thus the fault is that `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` does not internally handle the case where `getNullText()` is `null`. It expects that a "null text" string is set before appending a `null` object to avoid NPE.

No relevant clues were found in recent bug reports, which are unrelated.

Summary: The bug occurs because the `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` method does not defensively handle a `null` return from `getNullText()`, leading to a NullPointerException when a null object is appended without setting a null text.

This diagnosis points to a missing null check and fallback default string in the method:
`StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadLeft(Object, int, char)`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
